speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, please describe your pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. When did you first notice it, and have you experienced any fever or joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since the rash has persisted for five months without resolving, have you noticed any specific pattern, such as involvement of your knuckles or elbows? Additionally, have you experienced any fatigue, muscle weakness, or hair loss recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Dermatomyositis. While the patient denies systemic symptoms like fever or joint pain, the specific combination of a chronic pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities in a young female is highly suggestive of the heliotrope rash or Gottron's papules associated with this autoimmune myopathy. I will now request specific laboratory tests to confirm muscle enzyme elevation and check for associated antibodies. REQUEST TEST: CK (Creatine Kinase), ASR (Antinuclear Antibody), ALP (Alkaline Phosphatase).
